comparison: Both evaluate the same methodological claims (C2-C46). OpenEval finds the approach SUPPORTED with rigorous controls and validation. Peer reviewers rate it UNCERTAIN, acknowledging the methodology but raising significant concerns about resolution, sensitivity, and the technique's ability to detect dense axon morphologies compared to other viral tracing methods.

Both address Cre-line characterization and laminar distributions (C4-C9, C47-C55). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED based on anatomical patterns and literature consistency. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the laminar characterization with appropriate controls, though requesting more specific GENSAT line nomenclature.

OpenEval R3 evaluates quantitative sample size data (C56-C62) as SUPPORTED with modest but reasonable n. Peer R2 partially overlaps these claims, accepting the characterization methodology but not specifically addressing sample size adequacy concerns.

Both evaluate detailed projection patterns (C10, C63-C89). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with internal consistency and alignment with organizational principles. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, affirming findings as consistent with existing literature and noting valuable new insights on layer-specific outputs.

Both address correlation analyses between SSp-bfd and SSs (C11, C90-C92, C128). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on quantitative correlation approaches. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, accepting the similarity findings and highlighting new insights on differences between primary and secondary somatosensory areas.

Both evaluate topographic organization claims (C93-C108, C129-C132). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical tests and strong correlations. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, affirming this as a novel contribution showing topographic organization between somatosensory and motor cortices.

OpenEval R7 addresses striatal projection patterns (C109-C111) as SUPPORTED. Peer R5 includes these claims in their broader topographic evaluation, also rating SUPPORTED without specific challenge to the striatal gradient findings.

Both evaluate functional validation experiments (C12-C14, C112-C117, C120). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with significant correlations and consistency between anatomical and functional data. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, explicitly praising the functional validation as a key methodological strength.

OpenEval R9 evaluates synthesis claims (C118-C127) as SUPPORTED, noting agreement with established principles. Peer R3 includes some overlapping claims (C121-C127) in their broader projection pattern evaluation, also rating SUPPORTED and affirming consistency with literature.

Both address claims about extending current knowledge (C118-C119). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED based on high-sensitivity detection and brain-wide analysis. Peer reviewers rate UNSUPPORTED, directly challenging that the methodology extends knowledge, noting other studies have achieved similar or better resolution and specificity.

Both evaluate background/contextual claims (C1, C16-C35, C133). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, affirming the introduction provides clear context and is well-written. These are accepted background claims rather than contested findings.

Both address acknowledgment of study limitations regarding genetic markers and cell class diversity (C134-C138). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as appropriate contextualization. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, not challenging these limitations and implicitly supporting concerns about neuronal diversity.

Both evaluate methodological limitations regarding sparse vs. dense axon detection (C139-C141). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as honest acknowledgment of bias. Peer reviewers also rate SUPPORTED, affirming these limitations align with their concerns about resolution and precision, noting authors appropriately identify and discuss these constraints.

Both address methodological contributions and future applications (C15, C142). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED regarding integration of approaches and dataset utility. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, giving mixed assessments that acknowledge the methodology's value while emphasizing significant caveats about resolution and sensitivity limitations.

OpenEval R13 includes forward-looking claim C144 about future hypothesis-driven experiments, rated SUPPORTED. Peer R12 also evaluates C144 as SUPPORTED, with reviewers implicitly supporting the dataset's utility for future research and the research community.
